Lycopene, a highly lipophilic C40 isoprenoid, showed only 0.17% systemic availability in humans after ingestion of tomato paste; this supports low oral bioavailability for large lipophilic isoprenoids.
In a capsule study, only about 2.6% of a 38-mg lycopene dose was absorbed in humans, reinforcing low F for highly lipophilic isoprenoid molecules.

Phytoene, a flexible C40 isoprenoid, was estimated to have 58.5% absolute oral bioavailability in humans; this is above the 20% threshold but is less transferable because phytoene is smaller and lacks the quinone head.

One 13C-lycopene study reported 23.2% bioavailability for all-trans lycopene, slightly above threshold; however, most other lycopene studies report much lower values, and the result is formulation/label-dependent.
Hyperforin, a polyprenylated phloroglucinol, was described as having high oral bioavailability in an extract; this is contradictory but limited by smaller size and extract formulation.
